The codebase is intentionally NOT rustfmt-clean under the pinned toolchain (rustc 1.96.0 / rustfmt 1.9.0-stable, edition 2024 per workspace Cargo.toml). With no rustfmt.toml, the default `use_small_heuristics` chain-width of 60 disagrees with the hand-written style in many files — that is the mechanical reason the drift is so widespread. This is a hand-maintained house style that deliberately diverges from rustfmt defaults, not an oversight. Because rustfmt is not part of the enforced gate, pre-existing rustfmt-disagreement in tracked files (e.g. multi-line macro-arg wrapping style) never fails the lint gate on its own — amendment/review passes should not "fix" such drift unless it was explicitly flagged in the task, since touching it is unrelated scope creep.

PER-CRATE DRIFT CENSUS (each figure is a dated point measurement; treat as order-of-magnitude, re-derive with `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check` before relying on an exact count). Whole-tree order of magnitude: ~165 pre-existing `cargo fmt --check` diffs (2026-07-26).
- reify-stdlib ~946 diffs; reify-audit ~728KB of diff.
- reify-eval 149 files / ~37k lines — engine_eval.rs (~25 sites), engine_build.rs, elastic_static.rs, deps.rs, dynamics_ops.rs, engine_admin.rs.
- reify-compiler ~150 diffs (2026-07-27, base commit aa858e10a9) across expr.rs, geometry.rs, scope.rs, type_compat.rs, annotations/* and several tests/ files.
- reify-constraints ~90 diffs (2026-07-26) across solver.rs, registry.rs, relate_solve.rs, and most of tests/.
- reify-core and reify-ir both report diffs in many untouched files (2026-07-26): diagnostics.rs, dimension.rs, kernel.rs, ty.rs, value.rs (imports/enums).
- reify-kernel-occt ~150 diffs (lib.rs, ffi.rs, handle.rs, build.rs); reify-ir + reify-kernel-manifold (geometry.rs, constraint.rs, kernel.rs); reify-kernel-gmsh (build.rs, kernel.rs, kernel_real.rs, lib.rs, mesh_boundary.rs); reify-lsp; reify-solver-elastic (loop_closure_value.rs, loop_closure_solver.rs); gui/src-tauri (commands.rs, debug.rs, debug_server.rs, types.rs, main.rs, tests/rpath_smoke.rs, watcher.rs/watcher_tests.rs).

Rule: do NOT run `cargo fmt`, `cargo fmt -p <crate>`, `cargo fmt --all`, or any crate-wide/whole-file fmt for a targeted fix — it reformats the ENTIRE crate/file (observed up to 149 files/~37k lines) even when only one function needed a change, producing massive unrelated churn on every affected task. A red `cargo fmt --check` is a PRE-EXISTING repo-wide condition, not a regression you introduced.

Verifying your OWN edits introduce no NEW drift:
- The correct edition is 2024 (NOT 2021) — passing the wrong `--edition` flag flips rustfmt's style-edition defaults (import ordering etc.) and produces spurious diffs unrelated to your change.
- Preferred: `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check` (auto-reads edition from Cargo.toml). Flag ORDER matters: `cargo fmt --check -p <crate>` (flag before `-p`) has been observed to non-deterministically error "Unrecognized option: 'p'" or behave inconsistently (likely lock contention from concurrent cargo processes across worktrees) — put `-p <crate> --` before `--check`.
- To format only your own new/edited files, invoke rustfmt directly on those paths: `rustfmt --edition 2024 <paths...>` (equivalently `command rustfmt --check --edition 2024 <single-file>` to check). Note `cargo fmt -- --check <file1> <file2>` does NOT actually scope to just those files in this workspace — it still reports drift across the whole crate.
- Isolate your own hunks: `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check 2>&1 | grep '<FILE>:<YOUR-LINE-RANGE>'`, then hand-apply just those hunks.
- Deciding whether a flagged violation is actually YOURS: confirm the flagged construct is absent from `git diff <base>..HEAD`. Line numbers shift when you add lines above pre-existing violations, which makes old violations look new — the construct-level check is the reliable one, not the line number.
- CAUTION: bare `rustfmt --check <path-under-repo>` (not /tmp) can be intercepted by a shell wrapper/shim that prints a canned "LINT OK | rustfmt | 0 issues" regardless of actual state — untrustworthy. Also, the locally-installed rustfmt version can differ from whatever formatted the repo, producing whole-workspace false-positive diffs (confirmed by diffing a pristine base-commit file copy) — a local-toolchain artifact, not a real regression.
- To isolate a genuine semantic change from incidental reflow noise in the same diff (e.g. an accidental broad `cargo fmt` got mixed into WIP): normalize BOTH old and new file versions through `rustfmt --edition 2024` and diff the normalized versions (collapses formatting-only hunks to nothing), then splice that delta by line-range onto the real unformatted original file rather than committing the fully-reformatted file.
- Real gate: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` (or `--tests`) scoped to the touched crate. Rely on `cargo test` + this clippy invocation for verification, not fmt-check.
- CLIPPY COROLLARY: because the gate is `-D warnings`, rustc lints like `dead_code` are HARD ERRORS. An unused `pub(crate)` helper or struct field added ahead of the step that consumes it needs a targeted `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a comment, not a bare declaration.
- Confirm no NEW drift from your edit: diff `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check | grep "^Diff in"` site counts before/after your change, or check your changed line ranges are disjoint from reported drift, or diff `git status` before/after.
- Special case — verbatim relocation refactors (e.g. moving `#[cfg(test)]` module bodies to sibling files): do NOT dedent/reformat at all; relocate byte-for-byte (raw-string literals `r#"..."#` can be corrupted by blind sed-dedent). Prove faithfulness via identical sorted `cargo nextest list` output/count, not re-indentation.

content:
DRIVING THE reify-gui DEBUG MCP — CANONICAL (consolidates 9 entries, 2026-05-09..2026-07-26, under curator gate esc-5561-1). Companion: the gotcha appendix, topic=reify-debug-mcp-gotchas. DIFFERENT TOPIC, do not merge: ADDING a tool to this MCP is topic=reify-debug-mcp-tool-addition (gate esc-5563-1).

PORT CONTRACT — READ THIS FIRST; SEVERAL RETIRED ENTRIES WERE WRONG ABOUT IT. The port is PER-WORKTREE, not a fixed singleton. `scripts/setup-worktree-debug-port.sh` resolves it once and writes it to BOTH `.mcp.json` AND stdout (bare integer; diagnostics on stderr) — the two consumers must agree or esc-4202-61 recurs — and `git update-index --skip-worktree`s .mcp.json so the ephemeral port never lands in a commit. Server-side, `resolve_debug_port()` (gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs) reads `REIFY_DEBUG_PORT`, defaulting to 3939. AUTHORITY: CLAUDE.md and that script's header — NOT this entry, and never a hardcoded 3939.
HISTORICAL, NOW FALSE: entries written 2026-06-04 described :3939 as a fixed singleton that "cannot be redirected", concluded a worktree could not run a GUI acceptance unless it owned :3939, and prescribed parking on a human decision or escalating infra_issue. That gap is CLOSED — task 4340 (resolve_debug_port/REIFY_DEBUG_PORT) and task 4345 (the MCP-pins-a-shared-port gap) are both DONE, verified 2026-07-27. Do not park a GUI acceptance on port contention; provision your own port.

ENDPOINT: `POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` — the `/mcp` path, NOT the bare host:port. Route defined in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs (`.route("/mcp", post(handle_mcp))`). Same convention as the reify-permission server.

TRANSPORT — plain curl works, and needs less than you would expect:
- Headers: `Content-Type: application/json` AND `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. The Accept header is REQUIRED; omitting text/event-stream fails.
- Body: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":N,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}}`.
- NO initialize handshake and NO Mcp-Session-Id header are needed — stateless POSTs work fine (verified 2026-07-22).
- This is the ONLY route when the `mcp__reify-debug__*` tools are not registered in your agent session: the session's .mcp.json entry binds only if the port was already listening at session start, so a GUI you launch mid-session never registers.
- DOUBLE-DECODE THE RESULT: `result.content[0].text` is itself a JSON string needing a second parse. For `screenshot`, the image arrives as `result.content[0].data` = base64 PNG — decode to a file and Read it.

TOOL INVENTORY: `health`, `open_file{path: ABSOLUTE}`, `wait_for_idle{timeout_ms}`, `engine_state`, `mesh_stats`, `store_state`, `editor_content`, `fit_to_view`, `set_camera{position:[x,y,z], target:[x,y,z]}` (metres, world), `screenshot`, `demand_dispatch`, keyboard/list_elements, and `tools/list` to discover schemas live rather than trusting this list.

BEST ASSERTIONS: `store_state` → `viewports["design-main"].meshCount` is the single best "how many bodies actually render" signal. `mesh_stats` lists every mesh the engine emitted with entity_path — compare against meshCount to prove hidden != absent.

LAUNCH RECIPES
- Fresh dev GUI: `REIFY_DEBUG=1 REIFY_DEBUG_PORT=<free port> scripts/run-gui-dev.sh <file.ri>`.
- SECOND INSTANCE WITHOUT A BUILD — reuse an existing built binary and the already-running vite (port 1420 serves any instance): `cd /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/personal/gui-dev && setsid nohup env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib REIFY_DEBUG=1 REIFY_DEBUG_PORT=<free port> target/debug/reify-gui <absolute .ri path>`. The .ri file is pure data, so it may live in a different worktree from the binary — but check the BINARY's tree parses it first (its own `target/debug/reify check`).
- AMORTISE THE BUILD: `open_file{path}` + `wait_for_idle` loads a DIFFERENT example into the ALREADY-RUNNING GUI, so checking N examples costs one build, not N. Worth planning around: a cold debug build (feature `gui`) took ~25 min in a warm lane — launch it detached early and poll while doing other verification.

OWNERSHIP DISCIPLINE — still fully in force even though the port gap is closed:
- NEVER touch a GUI process or port you did not launch. Check `pgrep reify-gui` and listening ports before killing anything. A foreign GUI may be a human's dogfood session with unsaved work.
- ALWAYS ownership-check `editor_content.activeFile == your opened fixture` before asserting. Under concurrent worktrees another GUI runs a different branch's frontend and will not reflect your changes.

WHICH HARNESS FOR AN ACCEPTANCE GATE: prefer the H0 e2e harness on a free port over the agent's own reify-debug MCP client — drive it via the `rpc<T>()` JSON-RPC envelope in gui/test/visual/run.ts (it reads REIFY_DEBUG_PORT). The e2e suite's value-assertion scenarios live in gui/test/visual/assertions.ts (VALUE_SCENARIOS), each guarded by a "present and unique" structural test in assertions.test.ts; the behavioural signal runs via `npm run test:e2e` (= `tsx test/visual/run.ts value`) against a real reify-gui. NOTE it is NOT CI-gated (no .github/workflows; per the reify-debug-mcp-expansion PRD §5) — so it only runs when someone runs it.

reify: `CompiledModule.functions` is USER-SOURCE-ONLY — the test-harness trap it creates. CANONICAL (merges 3bd4fc1e + 2180e5df + 9d229441; verified against the tree 2026-07-27).

THE FACT: `compile_source_with_stdlib` does NOT put stdlib/prelude `pub fn` bodies into `CompiledModule.functions`. `crates/reify-compiler/src/compile_builder/functions_phase.rs` (~:95-105) builds a SEPARATE list for compile-time overload dispatch — `ctx.resolution_functions = merge_prelude_functions(&ctx.functions, &prelude_fns)` — under an in-source comment that states the rule outright: "`ctx.functions` (user-only) remains the output stored in CompiledModule". `ctx.functions` is what gets moved into the built `CompiledModule { .., functions: self.functions, .. }` in compile_builder/ctx.rs (~:195-205); `resolution_functions` is used for resolution only and then discarded. (Cite the SYMBOLS — `functions_phase`'s prelude-merge block and `Ctx::into_compiled_module` — the line numbers drift; the comment itself lives in functions_phase.rs, NOT in ctx.rs, which earlier entries mis-attributed.)

PROBE that establishes it: a fixture with zero user `fn` items compiles with 0 Error diagnostics and `module.functions.len() == 0`.

CONSEQUENCE for tests using `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)`: the function table is EMPTY of prelude fns, so no stdlib `.ri` body ever executes. On a lookup miss `eval_user_function_call` returns `Value::Undef` (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs ~:1625). Two things follow:
- Such a test CANNOT observe a stdlib `.ri` body's return value, and a name+arity intercept in reify-expr `eval_expr` cannot be "beaten" by the `.ri` body — removing the intercept yields `Value::Undef`, never the `.ri` placeholder's value.
- Therefore a test asserting `Value::Undef` is a NO-OP GUARD: it merely agrees with the fallthrough. RULE: under this harness a fixture discriminates iff the INTERCEPT's expected value is NOT `Undef`. This invalidated the "placeholder .ri body would return X" framing in crates/reify-expr/tests/option_recovery_eval_tests.rs (including the "coincidentally correct" note at ~:575-584) and in the task-5410 drift-guard doc comments.

PRODUCTION DIFFERS: `reify_eval::merge_functions` (crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs ~:1425, `pub(crate)`) unconditionally appends prelude fns into the runtime dispatch table, so stdlib `.ri` bodies genuinely compete there. Any test that needs a `.ri` body to actually shadow/compete must go through reify-eval (Engine / merge_functions), NOT `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)`.

CAPABILITY GAP worth knowing before you try to build the merged table yourself: `reify_compiler::merge_prelude_functions` (crates/reify-compiler/src/lib.rs ~:332) IS `pub`, but there is no public accessor exposing the compiled prelude's `CompiledFunction` slice to feed it — so an out-of-crate caller cannot reconstruct the production table from the compiler API alone.

reify HARNESS-LAYOUT GATE — MECHANICAL APPENDIX: the C1 harness-move how-to and every gotcha that has bitten. Companion to the canonical decision rule (topic=harness-layout-gate-decision-rule); read that first to decide WHETHER to move. This entry is only about HOW. Consolidated 2026-07-27 (curator gate esc-5534-1) from e17a20d2 + c77d25d9 + 4743c358, which were themselves already the product of two prior merges (1ef291b0, 309320f8). PRD merge-gate-compile-cost.md §5 C1 / W1; verified pattern from task #5278 (reify-eval EVAL-1), applicable to the same leaves (EVAL-1/2/3, CMP-1/2, C-cli / C-syntax / C-occt).

THE MOVE: `git mv crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs crates/<c>/tests/harness_<sub>/<f>.rs`, then declare it in `tests/harness_<sub>.rs` with `#[path = "harness_<sub>/<f>.rs"] mod <f>;`. The explicit `#[path]` is MANDATORY — a bare `mod <f>;` at an integration-test crate root resolves to the sibling `tests/<f>.rs`, not the subdir.

SELECTION IS PRESERVED: the move prefixes every test's nextest name with `<f>::`, so `test(/^<f>::/)` selects exactly that former binary's tests. Consolidation is selection-neutral because no `.config/nextest.toml` or tests/infra filterset references reify-eval test files by name — only the 7 override binaries use `binary()`.

GOTCHAS, each of which has cost a debugging cycle:
1. SOURCE-RELATIVE INCLUDES need exactly one extra `../` when the file moves one directory deeper (fixtures/ → ../fixtures/; ../../../examples/ → ../../../../examples/). `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), ...)` loads are move-safe and must NOT be touched. A successful `cargo nextest list -p <crate>` already PROVES include-path correctness, since `include_str!` resolves at compile time.
2. SHARED `tests/common/mod.rs` BREAKS. A helper referenced via bare `mod common;` now resolves relative to the new subdir (`harness_<sub>/<f>/common.rs`). Fix: `#[path = "../common/mod.rs"] mod common;` — relative to the submodule's new directory. Precedent: crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_geometry.rs.
3. A FILE `include!()`d FROM A src `#[cfg(test)]` BLOCK MUST NOT BE MOVED — moving it breaks the src-side include. Copy it in place instead of consolidating it. Example: crates/reify-eval/src/compute_targets/elastic_static.rs `include!`s tests/as_printed_zones_test_fixtures.rs.
4. GLOBAL-ALLOCATOR FILES MUST STAY STANDALONE. Any file installing a process-wide `#[global_allocator]` (e.g. common::alloc_counter::CountingAllocator) stays top-level AND grandfathered in the baseline manifest: two in one binary is a "multiple global allocators" compile error, and one shared allocator corrupts sibling alloc-count deltas.
5. RATCHET, SAME DIFF: remove each moved file's `crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs` row from tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest in the SAME commit. (Stated in the canonical too — it is the single most commonly forgotten step.)
6. Crate-level `#![allow(...)]` inner attributes remain valid as module inner attributes after the move — no change needed.
7. reify-eval's Cargo.toml auto-discovers tests (0 explicit `[[test]]` entries), so no Cargo.toml edit is needed when adding or moving harness files.

COST GOTCHA: alternating `cargo nextest list --workspace` and `cargo nextest list -p <crate>` triggers full ~7-minute recompiles, because feature unification differs between them. Pick ONE invocation form and stick to it for the whole session.

PROOF OBLIGATION FOR A LAYOUT-ONLY CHANGE: the BT-1 total `#[test]`-fn count must be UNCHANGED (reify-eval was 4690 at the time of #5278). Worked example of a clean move, task #5342 commit 894377054c: two new helix-sweep tests moved with 0 content bytes changed — gate PASS added=2 violations=0, kloc-cap 16/16, clippy 0 warnings.

Cargo build-script freshness vs warm-lane mtime normalization. CANONICAL (merges 8b1f6943 + f2583656, with the relocation-sweep clause CORRECTED — that half was superseded by task 5630, which is now done. Amended 2026-07-27 under curator gate esc-5634-1, verified against scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh.)

THE CARGO MECHANISM (general, still true): cargo decides whether to re-run a build script by comparing each `cargo:rerun-if-changed` path's mtime against the mtime of `target/<profile>/build/<pkg>-<hash>/output` — STRICT `>`, at nanosecond resolution. That `output` file, not a separate timestamp file, IS the freshness reference. Consequence: anything that bumps an `output` file's mtime silently suppresses the rerun and links the previously compiled artifact, with no warning. Verified empirically 2026-07-27 with a throwaway crate: change a watched file, then `touch` its `output` 5 s newer → the build script does NOT run (stale artifact, silent); restore `output` 5 s older → it runs.

THE REIFY EXPOSURE (STILL TRUE — this is the finding that survives): warm-lane seeding defeats `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for TRACKED files. `scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh` bulk-stamps every non-`target/` file to 2020-01-01 (the D5 mtime-normalization block), while `target/` is reflinked with `cp -a`, preserving base mtimes. A 2020-stamped tracked file can therefore never exceed a 2026-dated `output`, so the base's compiled artifact is linked verbatim. Measured in _lane-37 (2026-07-27): tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js at 2020-01-01 vs four target/debug/build/tree-sitter-reify-*/output at 2026-07-27 01:14. The `_touch_git_delta` rescue re-touches only TRACKED files differing from EFFECTIVE_BASE_COMMIT and is skipped entirely when that resolves empty — a conditional mitigation, not a guarantee. Any build script whose correctness depends on rerun-if-changed of a tracked source is exposed; the dangerous direction is a FALSE GREEN, where a C/C++ or grammar change is verified against the previously compiled object. Context: task #5629 / esc-5392-1, audited across cc-based build scripts by task #5630.

SUPERSEDED CLAUSE — DO NOT REPEAT IT: both source entries asserted that "the seed's `sed -i` relocation sweep bumps build-script `output` files to seed-time". That was true when written and is NOT true now. Task 5630 made the links-metadata/OUT_DIR relocation sweep MTIME-PRESERVING: it captures `stat -c '%y'` before the `sed -i` and restores it with GNU `touch -d` afterwards, round-tripping full sub-second precision because cargo compares at nanosecond resolution. The in-source comment states the rationale — rewriting a baked path is a CONTENT correction, not evidence that the build script ran. It is deliberately NOT `|| true`-guarded, so under `set -euo pipefail` a stat/touch failure aborts the seed.

AND THERE IS NOW A FAIL-CLOSED POST-CONDITION: `_assert_delta_newer_than_build_outputs` runs at the end of `--fresh-checkout`, after ALL mtime-mutating steps (relocation sweep and the `env!()`-relink touch), so it observes final mtimes. It finds the OLDEST delta-touched path and the NEWEST `output` under the lane target and aborts unless oldest-delta is strictly newer. Abort → empty stdout → the caller falls back to a cold rebuild. Ratified as §9.5 inv.12 in docs/prds/warm-lane-pool-cow-seeding.md: no step in the seed may leave a build-script replay file at or after a delta-touched source's mtime.

DIAGNOSING AN INVERSION TODAY: since the seed no longer advances those mtimes itself, an inversion almost always arrived IN the cloned base (a clock step during the base build, or a `target/` promoted under an odd clock). In that case EVERY acquire against that generation aborts identically and the pool degrades to cold fallback until the base is re-promoted — `scripts/refresh-warm-base.sh --landed-commit <sha>`. Self-healing by backdating the offending `output` would be strictly conservative (an older `output` can only cause an extra rerun, never a stale link) but is a behavioural change to the ratified fail-closed posture, so it is tracked as task #5632 rather than done as a drive-by.

DESIGN GUIDANCE THAT SURVIVES BOTH: prefer content-hash staleness over mtime for any build script whose correctness matters, and republish the watched path's mtime when outputs actually change. Cite the SYMBOLS (`_touch_git_delta`, `_assert_delta_newer_than_build_outputs`, the relocation sweep's `find ... -name output -o -name root-output` walk) rather than line numbers — the source entries' `:745-749` / `:892-898` / `:388-409` coordinates have already drifted.

Architect plan `files` list = the WRITE-SET. CANONICAL (merges 7d0eec99 + bbd7cac3 + b54c5f0d + 5d7c4909 + 978b4167 + 59390607 + b81895b0; consolidated 2026-07-27 under curator gate esc-5560-1).

THE RULE: declare in a plan's `files` only paths the task will CREATE or MODIFY. A file the task merely reads, imports, calls into, or reuses unchanged does NOT belong there — record it in the `reuse` section instead. The `files` array drives concurrency locks AND the phantom-done / pre-merge gate, which flags any declared file left untouched by the branch commits and forces a narrowing pass (`update_plan_metadata(files=[subset])`, then `confirm_plan()` — note that calling `confirm_plan` during a narrowing pass files an escalation).

WORKED EXAMPLES, each a real over-declaration that had to be narrowed (kept because the shapes differ, and recognising your shape is the whole value):
- READ-ONLY HELPER ALREADY VISIBLE ENOUGH: task 5334 (δ cluster formation) declared crates/reify-eval/src/structural_query.rs defensively, but build_trait_registry / enumerate_descendants / expand_structural_query / apply_trait_filters / apply_cost_aggregation are already `pub(crate)` on main and callable from resolve_order.rs with no visibility widening. Dropped.
- REUSED-NOT-REINVENTED: task 4232 (generic-user-fns γ) reused entity.rs's `check_type_param_bounds` / `satisfies_trait_bound` from entities_phase.rs without editing entity.rs (INV-1: "reused from the structure side, not reinvented"). Dropped.
- "USE THIS SUBSTRATE UNCHANGED": task 3392 (MITC3+ shell) declared shell_kinematics.rs but only consumed `shell_kinematics::shell_kinematics()` read-only; the new interior-tying shear helper landed in mitc3_plus.rs. Dropped. TELL: if a plan step says "in X.rs (or Y.rs)" or a reuse item says to use a substrate "unchanged", that file is a read-only dependency.
- CALLED HELPER + THE lib.rs FALLACY: a new method calling an existing helper like `Engine::dispatch_compute_node` in engine_admin.rs must not declare engine_admin.rs. And do NOT declare a crate root lib.rs to "make the new pub method reachable from integration tests" — inherent `pub fn` methods on an already-`pub struct` are reachable with no re-export.
- SHARED TEST HARNESS PULLED IN BY `#[path]`: task 4738 declared crates/reify-eval/tests/common/differential.rs (a 96 KB shared differential harness built up by prior tasks) because it pulled it in via `#[path = "common/foo.rs"] mod foo;` and READ its constants/helpers. Reading a harness is not modifying it. The branch only touched engine_build.rs and the new selective_demand_beta.rs. Dropped.
- A CFG-GATE CITED AS A LOCATION: when a task description says something like "gate at crates/reify-eval/build.rs:59-63" (e.g. `has_openvdb`), that is almost always a REFERENCE to pre-existing shared build-script infrastructure the task CONSUMES via `#[cfg(has_openvdb)]` / `#[cfg(not(has_openvdb))]` attributes — not a directive to modify build.rs. Do not declare build.rs unless the gate logic itself changes.
- GENERATED/GITIGNORED ARTIFACTS — THESE CAN NEVER BE SATISFIED: tree-sitter parser artifacts `tree-sitter-reify/src/{parser.c,grammar.json,node-types.json}` and `src/.grammar_hash.stamp` are gitignored (tree-sitter-reify/.gitignore), generated from grammar.js by `tree-sitter generate` and auto-regenerated by build.rs. They can never be touched by a commit, so declaring them ALWAYS trips the gate; committing the ~63K-line parser.c also causes merge conflicts. For grammar changes declare only grammar.js (+ test/corpus + lib.rs).

THE ONE REAL COUNTER-PRESSURE, worth knowing so the rule is applied with judgement rather than reflexively: the architect narrowing pass is structurally constrained to a SUBSET of the originally-declared set. So over-declaring costs a narrowing pass (recoverable), while UNDER-declaring means a file that turns out to be in the change set can never be added to the lock post-hoc (not recoverable). Task 4222 (std.fields δ containment seam) hit this — branch task/4222 touched crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs (+76 lines) though it was never declared, and it could not be added. The residual convention from that case (memory 481fc42f): for in-crate seam work in reify-eval specifically, defensively declaring sibling `engine_*.rs` files may be justified when a dispatch/containment seam can fan out within the crate. Treat that as a narrow, reify-eval-seam-specific exception to the write-set rule, not a general licence to over-declare.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT LAYER — do not confuse the two: this entry is about the ARCHITECT's plan `files`. The /prd-decompose `metadata.files` "lock charter" is a different artifact with its own rule (name a file only where the task text gives a high-confidence anchor, otherwise `[]`; NEVER a directory), enforced by scripts/lock-charter-guard.sh. RETIRED HISTORICAL BUG + a negative design lesson worth keeping: "the reconciliation harness misroutes project_id='reify' to project_root='/home/leo/src/dark-factory'". Retired 2026-07-27 under curator gate esc-5564-1, replacing the incident cluster 1e3614d7 / 057d0baa / 3ac85fc6.

THE BUG (historical, 2026-04-25 .. 2026-05-02, five-plus confirmed recurrences): reconciliation stages ran Taskmaster calls against the dark-factory root instead of reify's, so every reify task lookup returned "No tasks found" — reify IDs run far above dark-factory's tree, which topped out around 1145, and that ID gap was the reliable tell. Concrete instances: Stage 3 run 6b3022c1 lost IDs 2333-2640; run d6a3361e lost 36 spot-checked IDs (2828-2832, 2914-2929, 2938-2953); tasks 2807/2816/2835/2800 vanished the same way.

FIXED, DURABLY, IN CODE: the task-1143 project-isolation work hard-binds project_root per project_id via a registry built from taskmaster.project_root + DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS. An unregistered project_id now raises UnknownProjectError PRE-FLIGHT with "no silent fallback to any path" (fused-memory config.yaml §"Project isolation (task 1143)"; class UnknownProjectError and build_known_projects_map present in fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py). Independently corroborated: no misrouting has been observed live in reconciliation runs since, and the cluster's own recurrences all predate the fix by nearly three months.

THE NEGATIVE LESSON — the reason this entry exists rather than a plain deletion. The retired prescription (1e3614d7) told the harness to QUERY MEMORY for its own project configuration at startup, validate the result, and "override any hardcoded defaults". That is an anti-pattern: it makes MEMORY authoritative over CODE for which project scope a stage operates against, so anyone able to write a procedural_knowledge entry could redirect a harness's project scope. It is, ironically, the exact shape a prompt-injection attack would take. The fix that actually shipped does the OPPOSITE — a code-level registry that fails closed on an unknown id — and is strictly safer. RULE: configuration that determines a process's authority or scope belongs in code, not in the memory it reads.

SECURITY FLAG CLEARED, and how: Stage 1 flagged 1e3614d7's imperative second-person "the harness MUST..." phrasing as possibly injected/fabricated. It is not. Direct payload read shows agent_id="recon-stage-memory_consolidator", user_id="reify", created 2026-05-01T18:54:52, with the same structured-metadata shape its siblings carry (remediation:true, finding_type:"missing_knowledge", harness_modification_required:true, priority:"critical"). It was written by the reconciliation harness's OWN Stage-1 consolidator, about its own bug, in that agent's characteristic imperative remediation voice. No external author, no injection vector. SECONDARY LESSON FOR THE TOOLING: Stage 1 flagged its own earlier output as foreign because it does not recognise its own writing style — check agent_id before flagging authorship, or this false positive will keep recurring on old remediation records.

DELETED as part of this retirement: 1e3614d7-76bd-40bd-9fe5-dd7930ebcab3 (the unsound prescription — its lesson is preserved above), 057d0baa-52aa-4627-9d3a-55f28347d51a (remediation-verification record), 3ac85fc6-ddc4-4f49-852c-d66d26262731 (5th-recurrence incident record).

STILL LIVE AND CORRECT — DO NOT TOUCH: aeaca2db-ffa1-4100-bf05-08fa1784af0a (canonical reify config: project_id='reify', project_root='/home/leo/src/reify'), 5afac8e4-07de-4aa7-af0a-1c0a3edc3796, 8f2ac95c-9612-4a96-9a2b-ad6883667f80. These state currently-accurate configuration rather than describing the historical bug.

reify: the `tracing` callsite-Interest cache-poisoning gotcha, and the TWO legitimate remedies. CANONICAL (merges 2200d20e + 524933e4 + 2eda458f; verified against the tree 2026-07-27). The three source entries appeared to contradict; they do not — they answer different questions.

ROOT CAUSE: in Rust `tracing`, callsite `Interest` is cached PROCESS-GLOBALLY, but `tracing::subscriber::with_default` is THREAD-LOCAL. A unit test that installs a capturing subscriber via `with_default` and asserts a `tracing::debug!`/`info!` event fired will FLAKE if any sibling test in the same test binary reaches that same callsite FIRST with no subscriber installed: Interest is cached as `never` and the event is silently dropped, so the per-test subscriber captures nothing. MEASURED (reify-eval, task 5075): 6 of 12 runs failed; two consecutive identical `cargo test` invocations gave opposite results; passes in isolation with `-- --exact`. Applies to reify's widespread `CapturingSubscriberBuilder` + `with_default` idiom (engine_purposes.rs, kernel_registry.rs, engine_edit.rs, compute_targets).

REMEDY 1 — MECHANICAL, when the tracing event genuinely IS the contract under test: call `reify_test_support::prime_tracing_callsite_cache()` at the top of the test. MECHANISM (crates/reify-test-support/src/tracing_support.rs, `prime_tracing_callsite_cache`): a `std::sync::Once` installs a process-global default `Priming` subscriber whose `register_callsite` returns `Interest::sometimes()`. `sometimes` disables the static never-cache, so `enabled()` is consulted per event and dispatch falls through to whatever thread-local `with_default` subscriber is active. Setting the global default also rebuilds the interest cache, so it repairs callsites already poisoned by an earlier sibling. This is a real, sufficient fix — it is already used in ~20 files across reify-eval, reify-compiler, reify-kernel-{occt,gmsh,manifold}, reify-constraints, reify-lsp, reify-solver-elastic, reify-mesh-morph. Do NOT dismiss it: task 5075's entry prescribed remedy 2 without acknowledging that this helper exists.

REMEDY 2 — DESIGN-LEVEL, and the DEFAULT PREFERENCE when the log line is incidental: assert on a deterministic non-global observable instead of on the tracing event at all. A test that only reaches for tracing because it is the easiest thing to observe is asserting on a global side-channel; give it a real observable. This is strictly better than remedy 1 where it applies, because it removes the process-global coupling rather than working around it.

ANTI-PATTERN (rejected, both entries agree): do NOT fix with `serial_test`, a global mutex, or `--test-threads=1`. That couples unrelated tests to a log line and serialises the suite to protect one assertion.

CHOOSING: is the tracing event part of the contract you are testing (a diagnostic that ships, an audited warn count)? → remedy 1. Is it merely the most convenient probe? → remedy 2.

TEST-SUPPORT PRIMITIVES (crates/reify-test-support/src/tracing_support.rs): `CountingSubscriberBuilder` — count-only assertions, registers any subset of {INFO, DEBUG, WARN, ...} plus an optional `target_prefix(...)` filter. `CapturingSubscriberBuilder` — message/field capture at a given level. `WarnCapturingSubscriber` is WARN-only and private; for INFO/DEBUG field capture, define a small inline subscriber in the test module mirroring the `MessageVisitor` + `Arc<Mutex<Vec<...>>>` pattern near tracing_support.rs ~:586-690. reify-test-support hand-rolls its `Subscriber` impls, so NO `tracing-subscriber` crate dependency is needed — only `tracing`.

INV-GEO-1 mesh-contract mock gotcha — CANONICAL (merges de782198 + 76f848f3). Status: the trap itself was FIXED 2026-07-26 by commit ef4187454d (task #5105 δ, "flip mesh-contract site 1 to enforce-by-default"); kept as the record of the contract, the trap, and the lesson.

THE TRAP (historical): `MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` in crates/reify-test-support/src/mocks.rs used to return a SINGLE OPEN TRIANGLE (vertices [0,0,0, 1,0,0, 0,1,0], indices [0,1,2]) under an in-source comment that misleadingly called it "a minimal valid mesh". It is not: a lone triangle has three boundary edges, so `reify_ir::geometry::Mesh::validate` REJECTS it under `MeshInvariant::Closed` (open_edges == 3) — identical to the manifold γ test's `bad_mesh`. Harmless only while the kernel-seam mesh contract was warn-only. Flipping the tessellate→ingest handoff in reify-eval ("site 1") to fail-closed enforce broke every test routing that mock through a BRep→Mesh conversion (e.g. cross_kernel_handoff.rs), on a contract violation unrelated to what those tests assert (routing, caching, attribute forwarding, rollback).

BLAST-RADIUS BOUND (still true, and the reason this was tractable): site 1 fires only on CROSS-kernel Mesh handoffs, not on single-kernel tessellate-for-export. Real OCCT tessellations (examples/, prj/) are valid, so the .ri corpus was expected clean — and was.

CURRENT STATE: the mock kernels now hand back `minimal_valid_mesh(with_normals)` — a closed, consistently outward-wound unit tetrahedron V0=(0,0,0) V1=(1,0,0) V2=(0,1,0) V3=(0,0,1), the smallest mesh that actually satisfies the contract. The misleading comment is gone, replaced by a doc-comment explaining why a tetra and not a triangle. CITE THE SYMBOL (`minimal_valid_mesh` / `MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` in crates/reify-test-support/src/mocks.rs), NOT a line number: the original entries' `mocks.rs:1794` coordinate had already rotted twice before this merge.

DURABLE LESSON: a canned mock mesh must satisfy `MeshInvariant::Closed`, or it silently opts every consumer out of the enforcing seam. When a mesh-contract check is made fail-closed on a path fed by a mock, the fix is to emit a closed mesh — not to set the contract mode to warn per-test, which is how the mock hid the problem for months.

reify-audit PTODO detector: running it from a task WORKTREE, and the two distinct invocation contexts. CANONICAL (merges d6cd4626 + 9f2d2ae6 + 676a4c57 + b65510b8; verified against the tree 2026-07-27). The authorities that cannot drift are docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §8 (grammar/taxonomy) and tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh (the executable gate) — prefer them over any flag list below.

WHY IT FAILS OUT OF THE BOX IN A WORKTREE: the CLI eagerly opens the orchestrator runs.db at startup — even for `--pattern PTODO`, which does not use it — defaulting to `data/orchestrator/runs.db`. `data/` is git-untracked and therefore ABSENT in every linked worktree, so you get exit 125 ("error opening runs-db ... unable to open database file"). Exit 125 is an infrastructure/setup error, NOT a findings count.

CONTEXT 1 — PRE-COMMIT SELF-CHECK (structural lanes only; this is what the gate actually ratchets):
  cargo build --release -p reify-audit && ./target/release/reify-audit --pattern PTODO --runs-db "$(mktemp)" --no-jcodemunch --project-root .
An empty 0-byte file is an acceptable `--runs-db` for PTODO (per test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh); `--no-jcodemunch` skips an MCP connection PTODO does not use. Exit 0 = no High findings; exit N = High-finding count. THIS MANUAL RUN IS THE ONLY PER-TASK FEEDBACK FOR THE GATE: scripts/verify.sh runs the tests/infra run_all.sh pool (which owns test_reify_audit_ptodo*.sh) only when DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge, so a per-task verify will NOT catch a bad `#[ignore]` cite. Rebuild first — reify embeds sources at build time, so a stale target/release binary silently probes yesterday's tree.

CONTEXT 2 — FULL RUN WITH THE LIVENESS LANE (detects `orphaned`, i.e. cites naming a done/cancelled task):
  reify-audit --pattern PTODO --runs-db /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db --project-root .
  with REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB=/home/leo/src/reify/.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db
Both paths must point at the MAIN CHECKOUT, not the worktree. Without REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB it looks for a worktree-relative ./.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, fails, and degrades to structural-lane-only, printing "tasks.db unreachable ... liveness (β) and inverse (ζ) lanes degraded". Keep `--project-root .` so file/git scanning still targets the worktree. Task-liveness resolution also needs fused-memory reachable (default http://127.0.0.1:8002/mcp) — which is why context 1 passes `--no-jcodemunch` and skips this lane entirely.

SCOPE FACT THAT RECONCILES THE TWO CONTEXTS (the thing worth knowing): the real verify gate, tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh, runs `ptodo-baseline-gen` under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` — i.e. DEGRADED-STRUCTURAL ONLY (confirmed 2026-07-27 at :226, :281, :314) — and ratchets live structural fingerprints ⊆ the committed (empty) ptodo-baseline.txt. So liveness-lane `orphaned` findings do NOT block the worktree verify gate; only structural `untracked` / `bare-ignore` / `malformed-cite` do. Context 2 is for auditing, context 1 is for passing the gate.

GRAMMAR (authority: docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §8): PTODO marker keywords are only TODO|FIXME|HACK immediately followed by `(` or `:` — regex `\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b\s*[(:]`. `RESOLVED(...)` lines are NOT markers. A canonical cite is `#` + 1..5 nonzero digits anywhere on the marker line. Terminal owners (is_terminal_status = done|cancelled) yield `orphaned` findings; blocked/pending/deferred are LIVE.

OUTPUT SHAPE: exit 0 = no High-severity findings; stdout prints e.g. "reify-audit: 0 findings."; stderr is a JSON array of findings — EMPTY when 0, so a JSON parse of stderr fails in the clean case. That is expected, not an error.

(Consolidated 2026-07-27 from d6cd4626 (2026-06-13, grammar/cite rule), 9f2d2ae6 (2026-06-18, verify-gate scope), 676a4c57 (2026-06-19, MCP reachability + exit/output shape), b65510b8 (2026-07-26, pre-commit self-check recipe). The gate that ordered this merge was unsure whether b65510b8 belonged, since it is a different invocation context; resolved by keeping BOTH contexts explicitly labelled in one entry rather than splitting — splitting is how this topic re-accretes.)
label: canonical

Background-task reaping on this host, and which wake mechanism survives it. (Supersedes cb02ce75; folds in the Monitor-vs-watch-loop measurement extracted from 97557618 per curator gate esc-5547-1.)

THE REAPING: the host sweeps this Claude session's harness-tracked background tasks roughly HOURLY — observed 2026-07-25 killing both the L2 watcher and a run_in_background sweep about twice an hour. Reaping is LOAD-CORRELATED, not deterministic: under merge-verify CPU saturation, background tasks and even `setsid nohup`-detached children were swept within ~1-2 min, while under light load the same polls survived their full 10-20 min cap.

MEASURED COMPARISON (2026-07-22, reify host — the point this entry exists to preserve): plain background-Bash watch loops (run_in_background curl-poll loops) get reaped within the hour — two consecutive watchers died as "stopped" — while the harness MONITOR tool survived full 1-hour windows repeatedly. FOR LONG POLLS, USE MONITOR, with ALL terminal states in its grep filter, and expect to re-arm on its timeout notification. Independently re-confirmed the same week: a run_in_background fetch+grep merge-landing poll was killed mid-wait while an equivalent Monitor while-loop survived and delivered the landing event.

CHOOSING A MECHANISM
- Long poll that must re-invoke the agent → Monitor (or ScheduleWakeup, which is reap-proof but only available in /loop dynamic mode).
- Long-running CHILD PROCESS that does not need to notify the agent (builds, the GUI, a merge-worktree reclaim sweep) → `setsid nohup script > log 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Give it a self-terminate guard (e.g. grep the watcher-<project> lease file for your own slug each cycle and exit when released) plus a MAX_CYCLES backstop, and have it write a status file per cycle the agent can poll. Note the caveat above: under heavy load even setsid-detached children were swept, so pair detachment with ground-truth re-checks rather than trusting survival.
- The L2 WATCHER itself must stay a normal run_in_background task — it needs the harness fire-notification — so it stays sweep-vulnerable by design. Relaunch it on each kill; the killed-task NOTIFICATION is itself the re-establish trigger.

DON'T MISREAD A DEAD WRAPPER AS DEAD WORK: a killed `/spawn` wrapper does NOT kill the spawned session. It detaches into its own terminal and keeps running, along with anything it spawns. Verify via `ps` and the session's result.md / session-registry entry — never the wrapper's exit code or "killed" status.

reify: simulating a NEXTEST-LESS HOST for tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh suites — one canonical decision rule covering all three known techniques. CANONICAL (merges e218437a + 29463217 + 669fadfa; verified against the tree 2026-07-27). These were NOT three competing opinions: they solve two different problems, and two of them are a base technique plus its refinement.

WHY THE OBVIOUS APPROACH FAILS: you cannot just drop cargo-nextest off PATH. scripts/verify.sh's probe (search for `cargo nextest --version` / `command -v cargo-nextest`, currently ~:1360-1420, task 4971 / esc-4959-57) deliberately DISAMBIGUATES "genuinely absent" from "present but probe failing": if `cargo nextest --version` fails but `command -v cargo-nextest` still resolves, it HARD-FAILS after retries rather than falling back to the cargo-test plan. And cargo resolves `cargo-<subcmd>` from `$CARGO_HOME/bin` in addition to PATH. And `apply_env()` re-sources `~/.cargo/env` (search `if [ -f "$HOME/.cargo/env" ]`, currently ~:877), re-prepending ~/.cargo/bin. So a half-measure gets you NEXTEST=1 or a loud hard-fail, never the graceful NEXTEST=0 fallback.

DECISION RULE
(A) You need scripts/verify.sh ITSELF to genuinely take the NEXTEST=0 fallback → hide cargo-nextest properly. Two variants:
  (A1) MINIMAL RIG — THE CANONICAL IN-REPO IDIOM, and the one anchored to an executable exemplar. Stub `cargo` on PATH AND use an empty temp $HOME with a restricted PATH excluding ~/.cargo/bin. A stub alone is insufficient; the temp HOME must be genuinely empty (no .cargo/env) or apply_env re-prepends the real bin dir. The WORKDIR/SHIM_DIR/TMP_HOME + `HOME="$TMP_HOME" PATH="$SHIM_DIR:/usr/bin:/bin"` idiom lives in tests/infra/test_verify_nextest_probe.sh (task 4971) and was retrofitted into test_verify_semaphore_wiring.sh's (1q) block by task 4984. EXCEPTION: for `--scope all --print-plan` alone, an exit-1-for-all cargo stub suffices on its own — no non-nextest cargo call is made — so the empty-HOME/restricted-PATH rig is only required once the fixture goes past plan-printing into an actual nextest-vs-test execution branch.
  (A2) SYMLINK-FARM VARIANT — use this instead of A1 when the suite needs OTHER tools from ~/.cargo/bin (task 5599 lineage; applies to test_verify_nextest_absent_suites.sh, test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh, test_verify_semaphore_wiring.sh, test_verify_offline_partition.sh, test_verify_compile_gate.sh). Build a symlink farm mirroring ~/.cargo/bin MINUS cargo-nextest, prepend it to the REAL PATH with the real ~/.cargo/bin element filtered out, plus HOME=<tempdir>. Two traps: (1) CARGO_HOME must NOT be exported to the real ~/.cargo, or cargo re-resolves cargo-nextest from $CARGO_HOME/bin and the plan flips back to nextest=1; (2) A1's naive `PATH="$STUB:/usr/bin:/bin"` strips ~/.cargo/bin WHOLESALE, which also removes the tree-sitter CLI and makes test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh's suite-start `ensure_tree_sitter_ready` gate fail 5 execute-mode sections (A/B/C/F1/H) for reasons unrelated to nextest. A2 exists precisely because A1 was tried and hit that.
(B) You are driving a tests/infra suite and want to change what THE SUITE believes without touching host env at all → sed a TEMP COPY of the suite (task 5548): `sed -e 's|^SCRIPT_DIR=.*|SCRIPT_DIR="'"$PWD"'/tests/infra"|' -e 's|\*"nextest=1"\*)|*"nextest=1-SIM-NEVER-MATCHES"*)|' -e 's|cargo nextest run |cargo nextest-SIM run |g' tests/infra/<f>.sh > "$(mktemp -d)/sim.sh"`. Sed 1 pins SCRIPT_DIR so the copy can live outside tests/infra yet still source test_helpers.sh and resolve REPO_ROOT; sed 2 forces the suite's NEXTEST_AVAILABLE probe to 0 so nextest-gated asserts SKIP (crisp signal, no expected-FAIL noise); sed 3 makes the plan-line greps unmatchable, mimicking the cargo-test plan such a host gets. NOTE this patches the SUITE's beliefs, not verify.sh's — it is the right tool for asserting suite behaviour, the wrong one for exercising verify.sh's real fallback branch.

DO NOT copy a patched verify.sh: verify.sh and the suites both derive REPO_ROOT from their own BASH_SOURCE dir, which forces scratch files into scripts/ and tests/infra/ where run_all.sh may pick them up.

(Consolidated 2026-07-27 from three same-day entries — e218437a @13:09 (B), 29463217 @13:18 (A1, itself already a merge of 7f62407b + bfe37dc8), 669fadfa @16:06 (A2, itself already a merge of 8a58d1e3 + 83b76875). Six entries on one problem in one afternoon; if you rediscover this, extend the decision rule above rather than writing a seventh. Line numbers cited are 2026-07-27 hints and have already drifted once — anchor on the greppable strings given.)

CONSOLIDATED round-2b, 2026-07-27 (curator gate esc-5610-1; supersedes canonical 64564dd5 — itself a merge of 11 entries per task 5022 on 2026-07-05 — plus 5 residuals; total lineage 16 entries. Re-issued the same day to fold in the FIFTH trigger signature carried forward from esc-5367-4): An architect re-invoked on a task/NNNN branch can find the committed TDD work intact while its `.task/plan.json` is LOST or DESYNCED. `.task/` is untracked/gitignored and filesystem-only per CLAUDE.md, so it never survives a lane re-seed (tracked-files-only + `git clean -xfd`, e.g. when the branch is rebased onto a new main tip; `acquire_lane` always re-seeds from base), while the branch's committed TDD step commits (`test(NNNN): step-K RED` / `feat(NNNN): step-K GREEN`, sometimes prereq tags like `pre-1`) survive on task/NNNN.

TRIGGER SIGNATURES (five; the fifth is a DIFFERENT cause with an IDENTICAL recovery):
1. Task metadata `reblock_guard` reading like "warm-lane acquire fault for branch 'NNNN' (seed/worktree...)".
2. An architect re-invoked and finding branch commits but NO plan.json.
3. Branch annotated "RESUME CONTEXT: this is a re-queue".
4. A requeued task surfaced with a DIFFERENT task's plan.json attached (a prior lane-occupant's, or an adjacent sibling task's), or a DANGLING `.task/plan.json` SYMLINK whose target `worktrees/.task-meta/<lane>/plan.json` is missing.
5. DESYNC, NOT LOSS — plan.json PRESENT and structurally correct but ENTIRELY UNMARKED (every prerequisite and step at status=pending, commit=null) while `git log main..HEAD` shows the work already committed. Cause differs (the implementer died after committing but before its first `mark_step_done`), recovery is identical. Worked example: task 5367 / esc-5367-4 — 3 prerequisites + 10 steps all pending, 10 commits and 1473 insertions across all 8 plan.files already implemented. This signature exists because 5367 matched NONE of signatures 1-4, so a reader checked the list, matched nothing, and did not realise the documented technique applied.
FIRST TWO COMMANDS on any architect re-invocation: `git log --oneline main..HEAD` and `ls -la .task/`. Then, if plan.json exists, check whether its steps are marked.

CORRECT ACTION: RECONSTRUCT a faithful plan.json mirroring the committed step structure — `git log --oneline main..HEAD` (or against the branch's merge-base) plus per-commit `--stat`/diff, or `git diff main...HEAD`, to map each commit to its step by touched files — then `confirm_plan()` and call mark_step_done per commit, letting the executor re-verify the already-GREEN steps rather than redoing them. Reconstruction is not busywork: it regenerates the artifact the orchestrator state machine needs for the task to proceed to verify/land. Verify premises against the live worktree diff (`git diff <base_commit>..HEAD`) before reconstructing; don't trust old commit-message "green" claims or a plan's analysis narrative blindly — re-run the actual tests/clippy first.

DO NOT call `report_task_already_done`: that path requires the commit be reachable from MAIN, and task-branch WIP is not. Concrete check before you consider it: `git ls-tree main -- <path>` — a branch-only commit does not qualify.

PARTIAL-IMPLEMENTATION VARIANT (important, and easy to get wrong): if the commits implement only PART of the task, plan ONLY the remaining gap — do not re-plan already-green RED tests — but STILL list the FULL task footprint in `create_plan` `files[]`, so locks and the phantom-done check see all branch-vs-base diffs.

WHEN THE LOSS IS INFRA, SAY SO: after reconstructing and confirming, file `escalate_info(category='infra_issue')` noting the plan-metadata loss, so the lane fault is visible rather than silently absorbed.

WHY RECOVERY DEPENDS ON COMMIT DISCIPLINE (structural note, esc-5367-4): `iterations.jsonl` is written at END-of-iteration, so a mid-iteration death leaves ZERO durable trace. Task 5367's recovery worked only because commit-message discipline happened to be good enough to reconstruct intent — a thin dependency. A per-commit heartbeat or incremental iteration log would make the trace exist by construction, and would help the LOSS class here too, since a heartbeat survives independently of plan.json.

Task-specific gotchas to check every time (kept separate as they carry unique detail):
- A "chore: save WIP before rebase" commit can contain a REAL step's full implementation, not just noise — always `git show --stat`/`git show` each WIP-labeled commit before dismissing it (task 4168, memory a5e8b6b4-10f5-4d43-8b7e-f0cadd54e7bb).
- TDD commits can be directly S1..SN-labelled enabling 1:1 mapping, with a WIP commit occupying the slot of the step whose label was stripped during rebase (task 4870, memory b28158fb-2bdf-408b-979c-03f71cc11520).
- Interleaved WIP-save commits and step-pairs that share one commit SHA both occur — use the last commit in such a sequence as the step's recorded commit (task 4954, memory 17b3b5aa-39b0-4750-b6b5-d552081ac563; also task 3965, memory 1ccfce69-dec1-4a6d-ad1a-81e0440107f9).
- Trailing WIP commits beyond the last clean step commit can be folded into one clean commit via `git reset --soft <last-clean-step-sha>` + recommit — verify `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` is unchanged before/after to prove no content was lost (memory 57af0b70-d339-49ea-a203-6732b588bf47).
- Extra WIP commits after the last named step can contain legitimate additional task-scoped hardening already absorbed into an existing step's description — these don't need a new plan step, just re-verification that they still pass (task 4942, memory a7e90820-babc-4d09-9a27-05a81222ed24).
- A prior LANE OCCUPANT's stale plan.json can be shown for the current task (task 4019 shown task 3932's plan) — verify plan.json.task_id matches the dispatched task (memory e44cd1f5-0696-4fa2-899b-842fc61368e6).
- A SIBLING task's plan.json can be shown instead (task 4855 shown task 4854's plan) — verify actual branch state (git log/rev-list) before trusting the shown plan (memory 7b0d9518-e1ee-4f3e-b86c-f62a399b709a).
- After an INFRA-failure requeue mid-implementation, a rebase during "save WIP" commits can rewrite SHAs, so a reconstructed plan's recorded SHAs for already-"done" steps can point at the wrong (later WIP/amend) commit — don't trust recorded SHAs at face value; cross-check `git log --format='%H %s' main..HEAD` against the plan's file list (task 4906, memory fe1e9c21-0b65-49a5-88b5-bed9225037fa).
- The branch can carry a COMPLETE TDD sequence with plan.json simply absent — reconstruct and `confirm_plan()`, nothing else needed (task 4971, verify.sh nextest-probe fix: 4 commits a70958eb80..0eb2201908 present, plan.json absent; memory b6b82b57).
- PARTIAL case worked example: task 5031 (gui-state-sync L2) had diff.rs + L1 lint + bridge.ts committed and only engineStore.ts frontend transport remaining — plan the gap, list the whole footprint (memory d5226000).
- Full-implementation-already-committed case: task 5146 — the whole task was already on the branch when the architect was re-invoked (memory 5f1c0d8f).
- DANGLING-SYMLINK signature worked example: task 5357 — `.task/plan.json` was a symlink to a missing `worktrees/.task-meta/<lane>/plan.json`; derive steps from `git diff main...HEAD`, confirm_plan, then escalate_info(infra_issue) (memory 5697ff2f).
- REBASE-ONTO-NEW-MAIN-TIP trigger worked example: task 5367 — the re-seed that wiped plan.json was triggered by rebasing the branch onto a new main tip; `git ls-tree main -- <path>` is the check that the commits are branch-only (memory 2b911b54). The same task later produced the DESYNC signature above (esc-5367-4).

reify-gui DEBUG MCP — GOTCHA APPENDIX: the ways it lies to you, and how to tell. Companion to topic=reify-debug-mcp-driving (read that for the port contract, transport and launch recipes). Consolidated 2026-07-27 under curator gate esc-5561-1; the measured items were verified 2026-07-22..25.

THE THEME: several of these produce a CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER rather than an error. Each one below has already caused at least one false conclusion in a real session.

1. `wait_for_idle` != SETTLED. It can return `idle_after_ms ~= 28` for a file whose async tessellation / geometry-query passes are still running. Measured: bottom_deck_split.ri reported idle, then SIGSEGV'd the process ~6 s later. After wait_for_idle, confirm via `engine_state` values AND process aliveness before concluding anything.

2. `engine_state.values` IS A LIST, NOT A DICT — a list of `{id, value}` dicts. A `.get('mass')` extraction therefore silently reads None and manufactures a "mass is missing" result. This produced a false alarm in-session. Index by scanning for the matching `id`.

3. `mesh_stats` / `engine_state.meshes` UNDER-REPORT large composed scenes (bug filed 2026-07-22). For completeness questions, SCREENSHOTS are ground truth. mesh_stats remains fine for "which entity_paths emitted a mesh" — just not for "is everything here".

4. NESTED JSON, TWICE. `result.content[0].text` is itself a JSON string needing a second parse. Forgetting this yields a string where you expected an object.

5. A DETACHED `setsid` LAUNCH HAS NO SHELL, so a native signal death prints nothing — the captured stderr log is simply EMPTY. Silence plus a missing process means a native signal, not a clean exit. Use a wrapper that echoes `$?` to a log for the exact signal: 139 = SEGV, 134 = ABRT, 137 = OOM-kill.

6. NATIVE-CRASH CAPTURE RECIPE (the MCP stays reachable under gdb, ~5 s startup lag, so you can trigger the crash remotely):
   gdb -batch -ex "set pagination off" -ex "handle SIG33 SIG34 SIGPWR SIGXCPU nostop noprint pass" -ex run -ex "thread apply all bt 12" --args target/debug/reify-gui <file.ri>
   with REIFY_DEBUG=1 and REIFY_DEBUG_PORT set, then trigger via MCP `open_file`.
   STACK-OVERFLOW SIGNATURE, worth recognising on sight: SIGSEGV at a function's ENTRY line, with reference arguments reading 0x0, in deep recursion on a "tokio-rt-worker" thread (2 MB stack). That is the guard-page stack probe, NOT a null dereference. Corollary: reproducing the same input successfully through the CLI proves only that the main thread's 8 MB stack was enough — it does NOT prove correctness.

INTERNALS, for when you are debugging the debug transport itself rather than using it: reify-gui has TWO distinct dispatch systems. (1) `mcp_context.rs::mcp_tool_call_impl` handles engine-locked `reify_*` tools (tested in tests/mcp_dispatch_tests.rs). (2) `debug_server.rs::dispatch_tool` handles the `/mcp` debug tools; its default arm delegates frontend-mediated tools to `DebugBridge::query_frontend` (debug.rs), which emits a `debug-request` Tauri event, awaits a oneshot keyed by id, and is completed by `DebugBridge::resolve(id, json)` when bridge.ts (gui/src/debug/bridge.ts `buildHandlers`/`initDebugBridge`) invokes `debug_response`. Unit-testing that query_frontend↔resolve round-trip needs `tauri::test::mock_app()` (MockRuntime), which requires DebugBridge to be generic over `R: Runtime` (it pinned `AppHandle<Wry>` when this was recorded) and the tauri `test` feature enabled.

NEVER match processes by a pattern your own command line contains — `pkill -f` / `pgrep -f` SELF-MATCH. CANONICAL (merges 86187cbc + 052bf682 + 90a10d71 + the pkill half of 97557618; four independent rediscoveries 2026-06-09 → 2026-07-25).

MECHANISM: `pkill -f <pat>` and `pgrep -f <pat>` match the FULL command line of every process — including the shell running your own command, whose command line literally contains `<pat>`. From the Claude Code Bash tool this means the tool's own wrapper subshell matches.

TWO DISTINCT FAILURE MODES, both observed repeatedly:
1. KILL self-match — `pkill -f phase0-run.sh`, `pkill -f load-sampler.sh`, `pkill -f 'cargo build --workspace'` all killed the issuing shell (exit 144 = 128+SIGTERM, or "Killed" mid-output). In a compound command the shell dies AT the pkill and everything after it never runs. `kill -TERM -<PGID>` is the same trap when the PGID is shared with the tool's subshell. Consolation: the intended targets usually still died correctly — only the reporting command self-terminated, and persisted log files survive, so just re-read them in a follow-up command.
2. CHECK self-match, which is sneakier because nothing dies — `pgrep -f "cargo build -p reify-cli"` used as a liveness probe reports "still running" FOREVER, because the checking shell's own command line matches. Cost ~40 min of wasted wall-clock on 2026-07-25 waiting on a build that had finished in 2m35s. Same failure inside `until pgrep ...` watcher loops: the loop matches itself and never exits. Same family as the probe-exit-through-a-pipe gotcha.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD
- Kill by PID: resolve first (`ps`, `ss -p`, or `pgrep` read into a variable), then `kill <pid>`. This is the general rule — never kill by pattern.
- If you must use a pattern, pick one that CANNOT appear in your own command line: e.g. the target lane's absolute `target/` dir path.
- Bracket trick for probes: `pgrep -f 'carg[o] build'` — the regex matches the target but not the literal text in your own argv.
- Better still, avoid process-matching for liveness altogether: grep the build log for `Finished`/`error`, or test the target binary's mtime.
- `pgrep -x cargo` scoped by cwd avoids full-command-line matching entirely.

SCOPE TRAP TO PAIR WITH THIS (separate entry 7b8da91e): in the warm-lane sandbox `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f` match command lines SYSTEM-WIDE across ALL worktrees and lanes, not just your own — a match can belong to an unrelated `_merge-*` lane's in-flight verify. Before treating any match as yours, check `readlink -f /proc/<pid>/cwd`. And per project norm, never kill watchers by pattern: an orphaned own-watcher is harmless.

UNRELATED BASH-TOOL GOTCHA preserved from 86187cbc so it is not lost with it: multi-statement Bash tool commands occasionally get mangled by the harness's eval-wrapper collapsing newlines between statements (observed: an invalid `tail -8`, echoes concatenated). Prefer one logical command per call or `&&` chains, and write `tail -n N`, not `tail -N`.

Reify compiler — do `Boolean{left,right}` operands carry `GeomRef::Sub` consumption edges? BOTH answers are right; the discriminator is the OPERAND'S SHAPE. CANONICAL (merges 7489bac8 + c759c53b, which contradicted only because neither named the discriminator). Verified against the tree 2026-07-27.

DISCRIMINATOR — `resolve_boolean_arg` (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_boolean.rs; cite the SYMBOL, line numbers rot) has exactly two exits:
- Operand is `self.<sub>.<member>` (cross-sub MemberAccess): the task-3441 cross-sub pre-check calls `try_resolve_cross_sub_geom_ref` and returns `Some((GeomRef::Sub(...), vec![]))` — a REAL Sub consumption edge, zero sub-ops accumulated. Eval seeds `named_steps["<sub>.<member>"]`.
- Everything else (a bare `Ident` naming a sibling geometry-let, or a `FunctionCall`): falls through to `compile_geometry_call`, returning `Some((GeomRef::Step(step), ops))` — the operand's initializer is INLINED as sub-ops and the sibling's NAME does not survive. Measured: for `param geometry = difference(body, holes)` the names "body"/"holes" appear nowhere in the compiled realization's operations (only `Sub("hole")`, from the Pattern arg, survives).

There is NO bare-Ident pre-check on the boolean path. The bare-Ident pre-check (task #4668) exists only on the Modify/Transform/Pattern argument path, in crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs — `scope.geometry_realization_names.contains(arg_name)` → `GeomRef::Sub(arg_name)`, explicitly "do NOT inline the initializer as a fresh sub-op".

CONSEQUENCE for `extract_realization_edges` (private fn in crates/reify-eval/src/deps.rs; match arms Boolean{left,right}, Modify|Transform|Pattern{target}, Sweep{profiles}, Isosurface{grid}; `GeomRef::Step(_)` is intra-node and skipped; Primitive/Curve/Profile carry none): its enumeration is COMPLETE for cross-sub operands and is NOT an oracle for sibling-let boolean operands. Scope the claim that way — both the unqualified "authoritative enumeration" and the unqualified "not a complete oracle" are wrong.

NAME CONVENTION inside `RealizationDecl.operations`: a bare `GeomRef::Sub` name (0 dots) is a same-structure sibling; a dotted name ("sub.member") is cross-sub — a namespace split safe by construction, since DSL identifiers never contain '.'.

COMPLETE name-level source, when you need every sibling reference regardless of shape: the value-cell layer. `TopologyTemplate.value_cells[*].default_expr` carries `ValueRef(ValueCellId{entity, member})` for every sibling reference. Caveat: a `: Rigid` structure's auto-derived mass/centroid/moment_of_inertia lets also hold `ValueRef(geometry)`, so a consumption scan must count only Geometry-typed cells as consumers.

`extract_realization_edges` is not re-exported through `pub mod deps`, so consumers outside reify-eval (e.g. gui/src-tauri) must mirror its match arms rather than call it — cite it in a comment so the two cannot drift.

ADDING A TOOL TO THE reify-debug MCP — CANONICAL (consolidates 9 entries, 2026-05-05..2026-06-09, under curator gate esc-5563-1). Verified against the tree 2026-07-27. DIFFERENT TOPIC, do not merge: DRIVING the debug MCP is topic=reify-debug-mcp-driving (gate esc-5561-1).

AUTHORITY, USE IT INSTEAD OF TRUSTING THIS PROSE: `gui/src/__tests__/debugParity.test.ts` mechanically extracts the ToolDef names from the Rust source (regex over `ToolDef { name: "..." }`) and checks frontend/Rust parity. It is the executable contract; this entry only orients you. If prose and that test disagree, the test wins.

WHERE THE REGISTRY LIVES — a persistent PRD-level misdirection worth stating first. The registry is `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs`: `tool_defs() -> Vec<ToolDef>` and `dispatch_tool(state, name, params)`. It is NOT in `gui/src-tauri/src/debug.rs`, despite several PRDs (GR-016 §2.3 inventory row, mesh-morphing.md cross-ref) and task descriptions calling it "the debug.rs registry". `debug.rs` houses the unrelated `DebugBridge` used for frontend-mediated oneshot RPCs. And there is NO `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_bridge.rs` at all, despite some task metadata referencing it (confirmed absent 2026-07-27).

THE RULE: a FRONTEND-MEDIATED tool — one that reads the DOM or Solid stores rather than the OCCT engine — needs only TWO touch points:
1. a `ToolDef` entry in `tool_defs()` (gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs) with name, description and an object-typed JSON input_schema;
2. a handler in the `buildHandlers(ctx)` map in `gui/src/debug/bridge.ts`.
NO new Rust dispatch match-arm is required. `dispatch_tool`'s default arm — `_ => state.debug_bridge.query_frontend(name, params).await` — already forwards any unmatched tool name to the JS bridge. Consequence worth knowing: a bridge-only handler works via `tools/call` without rebuilding the Tauri binary.

THREE EXCEPTIONS THAT DO NEED MORE:
- STATE-BOUND / ENGINE-OR-DISK tools get an explicit Rust arm, via the `run_on_engine` helper: engine_state, mesh_stats, open_file, wait_for_idle, load_fixture, the stateless morph stats.
- IMAGE-RETURNING tools (screenshot, screenshot_window, element_screenshot) must ALSO be listed in `is_image_tool()`, or `tools/call` will not strip the data-URL prefix and emit an MCP image content block.
- FRONTEND STORE FIELDS your handler reads must be added to the `DebugStores` type in `gui/src/debug/types.ts`. That type exposes only a STRUCTURAL SUBSET of the real engineStore — e.g. it lacked compileDiagnostics/tessellationDiagnostics until task 4297. A field missing there is a silent read failure, not a compile error in the Rust half.

TESTS
- Rust-side, for a frontend-mediated tool, just assert the tool_defs schema (object type, required fields) — there is no Rust behaviour to test. Precedents live alongside in debug_server.rs's own test module (tool_defs_includes_set_camera, tool_defs_contains_set_test_mode, tool_defs_includes_screenshot_window, is_image_tool_recognizes_both_screenshot_variants).
- Frontend bridge unit tests go in `gui/src/__tests__/debugBridge.test.tsx` — note the `.TSX` extension. Task metadata `files` lists sometimes say `.ts`, which does not exist.
- JSDOM GOTCHA: jsdom has no layout engine, so `getBoundingClientRect()` returns width 0 under vitest. A handler that needs visibility must use CSS visibility instead — this is why the `ui_outline` handler does.

LINE NUMBERS ROT — cite symbols. The retired entries pinned dispatch_tool's default arm at "~:481"; as of 2026-07-27 it is at :1069, with tool_defs at :35, is_image_tool at :1030, dispatch_tool at :1047 and run_on_engine at :1077. Grep the symbol.

Nine entries restating one two-step rule over five weeks; the differentiating content was entirely in the exceptions and the file-identity corrections, all preserved above. If you rediscover this, extend this entry or the parity test — do not write a tenth.)
